# Project Meru / Sumeru

> Sumeru is an open-source **modular ERP framework written in Go**. Every business function —
> contacts, products, CRM, sales, invoicing, purchasing, HR — is an *addon*: a folder holding a
> `manifest.json`, Go model definitions and XML views. The kernel discovers addons, resolves their
> dependencies, syncs the PostgreSQL schema, and wires menus and access rights. The interface is
> server-rendered Go templates with no front-end build step. Project Meru is the initiative;
> Sumeru is the framework it builds.

**Status: pre-alpha.** The framework runs and the lead-to-cash flow works end to end, but there is
no tagged release, no upgrade path between versions, and no test suite on the business addons.

- Site: https://projectmeru.github.io/
- Code: https://github.com/ProjectMeru
- Licence: dual — community edition under Apache 2.0, enterprise edition under a commercial licence
  (the enterprise edition does not exist as a product yet)

## Key facts

- **Language / runtime:** Go 1.26+. Requires PostgreSQL and nothing else — no Node, no Docker, no
  message broker, no cache, no external job queue.
- **Repository layout:** three `replace`-linked Go modules. `sumeru` (the core framework),
  `sumeru_addons` (the standard business addons), `sumeru_custom_addons` (your workspace, and the
  module you actually run the server from).
- **Kernel packages:** `core/orm`, `core/module`, `core/engine`, `core/server`, `core/event`,
  `core/sdk`, `core/scheduler`, `core/applog`, `core/cache`, `core/importgen`.
- **Addon anatomy:** `manifest.json` (name, version, depends, data), `init.go`, `models/*.go`,
  `views/*.xml`, `security/security.xml` and `security/sys.access.csv`, optional `data/*.xml`.
- **A model** is metadata — a `ModelName()` and a `Fields()` slice — which the kernel turns into a
  real PostgreSQL table. Records at runtime are maps, not structs.
- **Addons never import each other.** They integrate through an event bus (`record.created`,
  `record.updated`, `cron.tick`) plus registry lookups, so an addon works whether or not its
  optional counterparts are installed. The manifest's `depends` array drives install order only.
- **API:** JSON-RPC at `POST /api/rpc` with API-key authentication, exposing `search`,
  `search_read`, `read`, `create`, `write` and `unlink`. Access rights apply as in the UI.
- **Security:** groups with inheritance, per-model access rights loaded from CSV, and row-level
  record rules whose domains understand `$uid` and the active company.
- **Isolation:** one server serves one database. Multi-*company* is supported inside that database;
  it is **not** multi-tenant. Separate customers require separate deployments.
- **Schema handling:** derived from field definitions and synced additively at boot. There are no
  down-migrations; columns and tables are never dropped automatically.

## Addons that exist today

Core (in the `sumeru` tree): `base` (working), `mail` (working), `automation` (partial — cron fires,
server-action execution is unimplemented), `sumeru_ai` (placeholder UI hooks only, no language model).

Standard (`sumeru_addons`): `contacts` (working), `product` (working), `crm` (working),
`sale` (partial), `sale_crm` (working), `account` (working — the most complete), `purchase` (partial),
`hr` (partial).

**Works today:** Lead → won → quotation → sales order → customer invoice → posted, balanced
double-entry journal entries. Purchase order → vendor bill.

**Does not exist yet:** taxes, payments and reconciliation, computed order totals, inventory or
warehouses, manufacturing, printable reports and financial statements, automated tests on the
business addons.

## Installing and running

```bash
psql -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE sumeru;"
cd sumeru_custom_addons
cp sumeru.conf.example sumeru.conf          # edit db_* and http_port
make replace-sumeru        SUMERU_ROOT=../sumeru
make replace-sumeru-addons ADDONS_ROOT=../sumeru_addons
make generate                                # regenerate addon blank imports
make run                                     # first boot → open /setup
go run . -- -c sumeru.conf \
  -i contacts,product,crm,sale,sale_crm,account,purchase,hr --stop-after-init
make run
```

There is **no default admin account** — the `/setup` wizard creates the first company and user, and
the email you give it becomes the login. `-i all` is rejected on purpose.

Creating an addon: `go run ../sumeru/cmd/sumeru-bp -name my_module -out ./addons`, then
`make generate`, then `-i my_module`. After editing XML, reload with `-u my_module`. Go changes need
a rebuild; adding an addon requires regenerating imports and rebuilding — there are no runtime plugins.

Server flags: `-c` (config path), `-i` (install addons), `-u` (update addons), `-d` / `--database`,
`-p` / `--http-port`, `--stop-after-init`.
